finalPrompt:
Create a NEW production RPG pixel-art WALKING atlas based ONLY on this visual character reference. Stocky short adult man Azar, russet red cap, dark black beard, ochre-yellow rough tunic, brown belt, dark brown trousers and boots, curved sword/scimitar. Restrained earthy pixel art, orthographic slight top-down. Transparent alpha background, no ground shadow, no grid, no labels. Exactly sixteen full-body character images in regular 4 columns by 4 rows separated with ample padding. Every character 37px-tall pixel-art equivalent, same consistent body proportions and costumes.
Four directions: row1 FRONT SOUTH, row2 LEFT PROFILE WEST, row3 RIGHT PROFILE EAST, row4 REAR NORTH. Within a row keep identical facing.
MOST IMPORTANT: four DISTINCT locomotion keyframes, opposed steps. Do not repeat the same foot position. In BOTH front and rear rows: column1 VIEWER'S LEFT BOOT visibly extends DOWN BELOW the right boot. Column2 VIEWER'S RIGHT KNEE bends up, right boot lifts off ground, left leg planted straight, tunic sways a little. Column3 VIEWER'S RIGHT BOOT visibly extends DOWN BELOW the left boot (OPPOSITE column1, swap the lower foot). Column4 VIEWER'S LEFT KNEE bends up, left boot lifts off ground, right leg planted straight (OPPOSITE column2).
LEFT PROFILE row: col1 near lighter-shaded left boot reaches FAR LEFT, far darker leg stretches back FAR RIGHT; col2 near left boot planted under body and far darker knee bent forward; col3 near lighter-shaded left boot stretches back FAR RIGHT, far darker leg reaches forward FAR LEFT, opposite col1; col4 near lighter-shaded knee bent forward with far darker boot under body, opposite col2.
RIGHT PROFILE row: col1 near lighter-shaded right boot reaches FAR RIGHT, far darker leg stretches back FAR LEFT; col2 near lighter-shaded leg planted under body and far darker knee bends forward; col3 near lighter-shaded right boot stretches back FAR LEFT, far darker leg reaches forward FAR RIGHT, opposite col1; col4 near lighter-shaded knee bends forward with far darker boot under body, opposite col2. Subtle shading distinguishes near and far leg. Arms counter-swing visibly with each alternate step. Keep sword held low consistently but allow its hand to move naturally. Keep face/cap/torso identity. No rigid standing floats, no duplicate col1/col3 or col2/col4. All frames must show a genuinely different leg configuration.
